rubric.text: Prove the periodic case: uniformly continuous on a compact period, then translate
Give a named counterexample for each false statement

solution:
Periodic and continuous: $f$ is uniformly continuous on the compact interval $[0,2T]$ (unif-cont). Any two points within $\delta<T$ lie in a common translate of that interval, so one $\delta$ works everywhere.
False: $x^n$ (pointwise limit discontinuous); $\sqrt{x^2+1/n^2}\to|x|$ uniformly (unif-conv); $(-1)^n/\sqrt n$ (square series diverges); $\sin x^2$ (bounded, not uniformly continuous).
